findings.title: Queries are interpolated twice in the shard-splitting flow
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery now interpolates each query (line 49-52), then passes the already-interpolated targets into splitQueriesByStreamShard. For every shard group, runNextRequest (line 163) calls runSplitQuery(datasource, subRequest, ...) with that subRequest, and the new runSplitQuery in querySplitting.ts (line 296-299) re-applies datasource.applyTemplateVariables to the same queries. The result is 1 + N interpolations of the same queries (N = number of shard groups). The test on line 112 of shardQuerySplitting.test.ts even pins this in place with expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5). It works only because the template-service replacement is idempotent on the substituted values, but it is wasted work on every shard group iteration, and any future interpolation that is not strictly idempotent (e.g. counters, suffixes, timestamps) will silently produce wrong results or repeated side effects on the same query objects.

findings.title: Brittle call-count assertion masks the duplicate-interpolation waste
findings.body: The test pins expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5), which depends on the exact number of shard groups produced by the specific fetchLabelValues fixture plus the 1+N pattern above. Any change to grouping size, fetchLabelValues results, or the runSplitQuery call sites will break this test even when the user-visible behavior is correct. The assertion exists only to document the redundant call from runShardSplitQuery through runSplitQuery; it should instead verify the intended contract (e.g. that queries are interpolated exactly once before the first runQuery call) so a regression that introduces or removes duplicate interpolation is caught.
